description:
A car against an inverted surface. Then a brief airborne maneuver. Tesla says fan suction and cold-gas thrust do different jobs. Pressure can hold it against a surface; expelled gas can change its motion. A short maneuver is not proof of sustained practical flight.

Original Magnivis reconstruction and qualitative physics animation, not Tesla demonstration footage. Approximate exterior, force directions and motion; no proprietary hardware layout or measured flight duration. Synthetic narration; original synthesized sound.

Reported reveal: Car and Driver; Electrek. Fans and cold-gas thrusters: claims attributed to Tesla, not independently tested here. General physics: NASA, OpenStax and McMurtry's separate fan-car demonstration. Sources:
https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a74145531/tesla-roadster-revealed/
https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a74165059/tesla-roadster-thrusters-fan-system-explained/
https://electrek.co/2026/10/15/an-updated-technical-look-at-teslas-kick-flipping-0-60-in-1s-next-gen-roadster/
https://mcmurtry.com/upside-down-driving/
https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/thrust/
https://www.nasa.gov/smallsat-institute/sst-soa/in-space_propulsion/
https://openstax.org/books/physics/pages/6-3-rotational-motion
